newsitem.title: CHINA: China lashes out at U.S. congressman over HK.
newsitem.headline: China lashes out at U.S. congressman over HK.

text.p: China on Tuesday dismissed as irresponsible a proposal by U.S. Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jesse Helms to bar members of Hong Kong's provisional legislature from visiting the United States.
"This is irresponsible behaviour," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing on Tuesday when asked to comment on Helms's suggestion.

Helms was considering introducing a bill to ban members of Hong Kong's China-backed provisional legislature from entering the United States after Beijing resumes sovereignty over the British colony at midnight on June 30, an aide said in Washington on Monday.

China has opposed democratic reforms in Hong Kong brought in by colonial Governor Chris Patten without its approval, and has vowed to replace the elected legislature with the provisional body when it takes over.
Shen described the proposal not to grant entry to the United States to members of the provisional legislature as "unreasonable".
"It would be a violation of international law and undemocratic," Shen said, adding that some people were now trying to politicise the Hong Kong issue.
The legislation has not been drafted so no details were available. If offered, it would have to be passed by both the Senate and House of Representatives and signed by President Bill Clinton.
Helms, a conservative North Carolina Republican, is a fervent anti-Communist.
